phUSDSupplyCap.question: Does the real phUSD (IFlax) have a supply cap?
phUSDSupplyCap.basis: lib/phlimbo-ea/lib/immutable/flax-token-v2/src/FlaxToken.sol:58-69. FlaxToken.mint gates on exactly two requires — minterInfo.canMint and minterInfo.mintVersion == mintVersion — then calls OZ ERC20._mint. There is no cap, no max supply, no ceiling of any kind. The only bound is uint256 overflow.
phUSDSupplyCap.consequence: Task hypothesis 3 (cap hit -> unbounded unpayable liability -> permanently-reverting pull) is REFUTED and does NOT apply. The bank is honourable: the ONLY trigger for a failed mint is loss of authorization (setMinter(false) or revokeAllMintPrivileges() bumping mintVersion), both owner-controlled and fully recoverable by re-granting via setMinter, which re-stamps the current mintVersion. Correspondingly, the 'bank is honourable but the uncapped-mint surface widens' branch is the live one — see dedup04Assessment: the surface does NOT in fact widen.

doesTheBankWidenTheSurface.verdict: NO. The bank is a STRICT SUBSET of the stream DEDUP-04 already governs, and cannot exceed it.
argument: MAGNITUDE: the catch block at :915 banks `pendingPhUSDAmount` — bit-for-bit the same value the success path would have minted at :913. It authorizes no wei that accPhUSDPerShare had not already accrued. banked + paid == earned exactly (proven: test_ECON003).

DORMANCY: the mint leg is guarded by `if (pendingPhUSDAmount > 0)` (:903). At desiredAPYBps == 0, pending is identically zero, so the leg is never entered and the bank is never written. The bank is dormant for EXACTLY the same reason, and under exactly the same condition, as DEDUP-04 itself. LEG 2 covers the bank with no gap.

LEG 1 CONSISTENCY: the bank is an IOU redeemable if-and-only-if mint privilege is active (a failed pull reverts and leaves the bank intact, :649). That is a literal restatement of 'solvency == active mint privilege', not a departure from it. LEG 1 is not weakened; arguably the bank makes the documented dependency more explicit.

NO NEW DEFERRAL POWER: the retroactive-mint-on-authority-restore property already existed BEFORE story-031 via `pending`. _updatePool advances accPhUSDPerShare regardless of mint authority, so under the old code a user simply held un-claimable pending across the outage and claimed the full backlog on restore. story-031 changes WHERE the crystallized amount is recorded (bank vs pending), not WHETHER it is retroactively mintable. Economically neutral.

reasoning: The banked amount is frozen in nominal terms at bank time and does not accrue further; the user's ongoing accrual continues independently against accPhUSDPerShare after the caller-side debt realignment. Banking neither compounds nor forfeits.

phUSD is fungible and non-rebasing, with no snapshot governance, no redemption queue, and no peg/redemption window reachable from phlimbo-ea's scope. Timing optionality over a fixed nominal amount of a fungible token confers nothing here.
Any timing optionality the bank grants was already available via `pending` (a user can simply not call claim). The bank is strictly no better than the pre-existing option.

findings.title: Migrator-delegated phUSD bank is credited to an address with no retrieval path, and — uniquely among the three banks — is unrecoverable on-chain by ANY mechanism, including emergencyTransfer
findings.description: Under migrator delegation, stake/withdraw/claim pass msg.sender (the migrator) as `beneficiary` (:708/:749/:806). A failed mint therefore credits `unclaimablePhUSDOf[migrator]` (:915) with a value earned by the USER, whose debt is simultaneously realigned to the full accumulator by the caller (:715/:761/:808) — so the value leaves the user's account permanently. The sole retrieval path, claimUnclaimablePhUSD() (:644), is strictly msg.sender-keyed with no pull-on-behalf. ADJUDICATING THE QUESTION THE PROFILE DEFERRED TO TIER 2 (LOCAL-001 boundaryNote): MigratorV2V3's complete external surface is seedUsers / migrate / migrateOne / skipCurrent / claimUnclaimable / withdrawAll / userCount. NONE reaches PhlimboV3's bank. `claimUnclaimable` (:302) reads the migrator's OWN `unclaimable[token][msg.sender]` mapping, not PhlimboV3's; `withdrawAll` (:318) sweeps `balanceOf(address(this))`. There is no generic execute/call. The migrator therefore CANNOT retrieve the bank. THE ESCALATION over the stable/promo legs: those banks are backed by contract-held tokens, so PhlimboV3.emergencyTransfer (:360-378) sweeps them to the owner for out-of-band redistribution. The phUSD bank was NEVER MINTED — there is nothing to sweep — so it is beyond the reach of every on-chain recovery mechanism the protocol has.
findings.economicImpact: The user's earned phUSD is destroyed on-chain rather than deferred: their pending is zeroed, they hold no bank entry, and the entry that does exist is keyed to a contract that can never call the pull. totalUnclaimablePhUSD is permanently overstated by the stranded amount, corrupting the protocol's only liability record (see ECON-Q-01).
findings.attackScenario:
No attacker required — this is an operational footgun, not an exploit.
1. Owner sets a non-zero desiredAPYBps (DORMANT TODAY — see dormancy).
2. PhlimboV3 loses phUSD mint authority (setMinter(false), or revokeAllMintPrivileges() bumping mintVersion).
3. MigratorV2V3.migrate() reaches a user who already holds a V3 position (the second-pass case), calling phlimboV3.stake(amount, user) at :256; PhlimboV3 auto-claims at :708 with beneficiary == migrator.
4. The mint reverts; pendingPhUSD is banked to unclaimablePhUSDOf[migrator]; the user's phUSDDebt realigns to full.
5. MigratorV2V3's balance-delta accounting (:260) correctly sees a zero delta and forwards nothing — so no double-pay, but also no rescue.
6. Authority is restored. The bank is now honourable, but no call path exists to honour it.
findings.profitability: N/A — nobody profits. Pure deadweight loss.
affectedParties: users migrated during a mint-authority outage (value destroyed)
findings.dormancy: GATED behind DEDUP-04's re-emit trigger. At the shipped config (desiredAPYBps == 0 by construction, src/PhlimboV3.sol:60) pendingPhUSDAmount is identically zero, the mint leg at :913 is never entered, and this finding is unreachable. Proven: test_ECON004_atShippedZeroAPY_bankIsUnreachable.

asserts: pendingPhUSD(alice) == 0 and unclaimablePhUSDOf(alice) == 0 (value left the user)
unclaimablePhUSDOf(migrator) == earned (landed at an address with no pull)
alice's own pull reverts 'Nothing to claim'
migrator's balance sweep (its only recovery) recovers 0 — the migrator holds no phUSD float, so any balance could only have come from the bank
the bank SURVIVES emergencyTransfer untouched; totalUnclaimablePhUSD remains permanently outstanding
pocEvidence.positiveControl: test_ECON001_positiveControl_callThroughRecovers — PASS. An otherwise-identical migrator that merely exposes `phlimbo.claimUnclaimablePhUSD()` recovers the full amount. This proves the strand is an ABI-completeness gap in MigratorV2V3, not an inherent property of the banking design — and pins the fix.

findings.relationship: EXTENDS ledger V3-L-15 (audit-10, 'migrator no-self-pull') and profile LOCAL-001 to a THIRD asset. NOT a fresh root cause — same class, new leg. DISCLOSURE: filed separately from V3-L-15 because the un-minted asset removes the emergencyTransfer backstop that makes V3-L-15's stable leg recoverable; that unrecoverability is a genuine escalation of the class, not a restatement. Recommend the deduplicator collapse the ROOT CAUSE into V3-L-15 while preserving the unrecoverability note.
findings.severityRationale: LOW, not Medium. Against: value is genuinely destroyed on-chain and unrecoverable by any protocol mechanism. For Low: (a) triple-gated — requires a non-zero-APY config that is NOT shipped, PLUS a mint-authority outage, PLUS migrator delegation of a user with an existing V3 position; (b) the owner controls FlaxToken and can mint the user whole out-of-band at zero cost, so the real-world loss is a bookkeeping error the owner can correct, not an unrecoverable user loss; (c) no attacker, no profit, no theft. C4 Medium requires function/availability impact or a value leak with stated assumptions — the availability impact is nil and the leak is owner-correctable.
findings.recommendation: Preferred: add a pull-on-behalf variant (e.g. claimUnclaimablePhUSDFor(address beneficiary) crediting the recorded beneficiary) so no address can hold an unreachable entry. Cheaper alternative: add a call-through to MigratorV2V3 (the positive control proves this suffices), though it fixes only the known migrator and not a future one. Structural alternative: credit the bank to `user` rather than `beneficiary` — but note this silently changes reward routing semantics and would diverge the banked path from the paid path, so it should not be adopted without a story decision.

findings.title: The phUSD bank survives the terminal ejector seat and remains a live, permissionless, un-pause-gated claim on FRESH phUSD supply after emergencyTransfer has swept and paused the contract
findings.description: emergencyTransfer (:360-378) is a BALANCE sweep: it moves phUSD/rewardToken/promo balances to the recipient and calls _pause(). It is the project's terminal ejector seat (story-022, recovery out-of-band). The stable and promo banks are neutralized by it as a side effect — their tokens are gone, so the pulls revert. The phUSD bank is NOT: it was never minted, so the sweep cannot see it, and claimUnclaimablePhUSD (:644) is deliberately NOT whenNotPaused, so the pause does not stop it either. As long as PhlimboV3 retains mint authority, every outstanding bank entry remains pullable by its holder AFTER the ejector seat has fired, minting brand-new supply that the sweep never accounted for.
findings.economicImpact: After a terminal wind-down in which the owner sweeps all balances and makes users whole out-of-band, holders of a phUSD bank entry can ALSO mint their banked amount from the dead contract — being paid twice, with the second payment creating un-backed phUSD supply.
findings.attackScenario:
No attacker required — a non-malicious owner walks into it.
1. desiredAPYBps non-zero (DORMANT TODAY).
2. Mint authority lapses; users claim; banks fill; authority is restored (normal incident recovery), leaving residual un-pulled bank entries.
3. Later, the owner pulls emergencyTransfer, sweeps every balance, and reimburses users out-of-band from the swept funds.
4. Residual bank holders call claimUnclaimablePhUSD() on the paused, drained contract and mint fresh phUSD — a second payment for the same earnings.
findings.profitability: Profitable to a bank holder only in the double-pay scenario, and only by the owner's oversight. No adversarial construction — the holder is claiming what the contract says it owes them.
findings.dormancy: Same DEDUP-04 gate as ECON-001 (desiredAPYBps == 0 => bank never written). Additionally requires a non-empty residual bank at sweep time.

asserts: after emergencyTransfer: phUSD.balanceOf(phlimbo) == 0 and phlimbo.paused() == true
alice's claimUnclaimablePhUSD() STILL SUCCEEDS on the paused, drained contract
phUSD.totalSupply() == supplyBefore + earned — FRESH supply minted after the ejector seat fired

findings.law3Analysis: IN SCOPE as a non-obvious owner footgun. The Law-3 test — 'would a competent, non-malicious owner be surprised by this consequence?' — resolves YES: the ejector seat is balance-based and visibly neutralizes the other two banks, which invites the reasonable inference that it neutralizes all three. The phUSD bank's survival is invisible precisely BECAUSE it is un-minted. This is not a 'malicious owner could' vector and is not reported as one.
findings.ejectorSeatPrincipleCompliance: This finding does NOT propose accounting inside emergencyTransfer and does not re-file pe7m2 (closed INVALID). The ejector seat's terminal, no-accounting design is respected as-is. The hazard is a liability that OUTLIVES the terminal action and lives entirely OUTSIDE it, and the recommendation is correspondingly a runbook step, not a code change to the hatch.
findings.recommendation: Operational, not structural: add to the emergencyTransfer runbook a mandatory follow-up step — revoke PhlimboV3's phUSD minter role (FlaxToken.setMinter(phlimbo, false), or revokeAllMintPrivileges()) — so the terminal action actually terminates the mint obligation. Document in SolvencyDetermination.md that emergencyTransfer alone does NOT extinguish the phUSD bank, unlike the stable/promo banks. If a code change is preferred over a runbook step, the correct site is a documented note at :644, not accounting inside the hatch.

findings.title: totalUnclaimablePhUSD is the protocol's only record of outstanding un-backed phUSD mint liability, and nothing reads it
findings.description: totalUnclaimablePhUSD (:181) is written at :916 and :648 and exposed via a public getter (IPhlimboV3.sol:457). No control flow anywhere reads it — not in PhlimboV3, not in MigratorV2V3, and there is no phUSD supply cap for it to interact with (FlaxToken has none). It is purely informational. Because the banked phUSD is un-minted, phUSD.totalSupply() UNDERSTATES the protocol's true outstanding phUSD obligation by exactly totalUnclaimablePhUSD. Any external solvency, backing-ratio, or supply monitor that reads totalSupply() — a live theme across the Phoenix system, cf. yield-claim-nft DEDUP-001 unbacked-phUSD — will therefore under-count. ECON-001 compounds this from the other side: a stranded migrator entry inflates totalUnclaimablePhUSD permanently, so the figure is simultaneously unread AND corruptible upward.
findings.economicImpact: No on-chain accounting is wrong today (the counter is not load-bearing, so its inaccuracy propagates nowhere). The impact is purely on off-chain solvency observability of an un-backed mint obligation.
findings.dormancy: Same DEDUP-04 gate — the counter can only leave zero once desiredAPYBps is non-zero.
findings.severityRationale: QA. No value at risk, no availability impact, on-chain accounting correct. Surfaced because it is the visible-channel record of an un-backed mint liability in a system with a documented unbacked-phUSD theme, and because it is the natural place to catch ECON-001 in monitoring.
findings.recommendation: Document in SolvencyDetermination.md that true outstanding phUSD == phUSD.totalSupply() + PhlimboV3.totalUnclaimablePhUSD() (plus any sibling banks), and have any external backing monitor read the getter. No code change required.

refutations.hypothesis: Task item 5 — a third party gas-griefs another user's claim into the bank via the 63/64 rule (forcing the try/catch to swallow an out-of-gas), profiting from the victim's deferral.
reasoning: REACHABILITY: all three _claimRewards call sites are auth-gated by `require(msg.sender == user || msg.sender == migrator)` (:697/:741/:791). A third party cannot reach ANOTHER user's claim path at all, so the 63/64 vector has no entry point. The only non-self caller is the migrator, a trusted owner-set delegate (Law 3).

INCENTIVE: on self-service paths beneficiary == msg.sender == the victim, so 'forcing the bank' means banking one's OWN value. The griefer would burn gas to defer paying themselves. Strictly negative EV.

HARM: even if forced, the loss is DEFERRAL not destruction — the bank is intact, honourable, and pullable (:644, un-pause-gated). The one case where it IS destruction requires beneficiary != user, which is the migrator case = ECON-001, not griefing.
NOTE: batchClaim is permissionless but forces payout to the STAKER and touches only the promo leg — it never reaches the phUSD leg, so it offers no third-party entry either.
refutations.pocEvidence: test_ECON005_thirdPartyCannotForceVictimBank — PASS. Bob (unprivileged) is rejected with 'Not authorized' on claim(alice), withdraw(1 ether, alice), and stake(1 ether, alice).

refutations.hypothesis: Task item 6 — story-031's banking causes Linear-Depletion rate/schedule drift (this project is the ORIGIN of that class; it recurred as phoenix-nft-staking run-18 M-01, and it is REPORTABLE here — not suppressed).
refutations.verdict: REFUTED for story-031 — the changed code touches NO rate-recompute path. The class is NOT re-suppressed; it was actively checked and is clean on this diff.
reasoning: STORY-031's DIFF touches only _claimRewards' phUSD leg (:913-918) and adds claimUnclaimablePhUSD (:644-651) plus two state vars. Neither writes totalStaked, rewardBalance, promoRewardBalance, rewardPerSecond, phUSDPerSecond, promoRewardPerSecond, or lastRewardTime.

STABLE DEPLETION: _updatePool (:825) still does NOT recompute rewardPerSecond — the V2 fix is intact, with the explanatory comment preserved at :848-850 ('V1 used to recompute rewardPerSecond here. V2 deliberately does not — that was the bug'). Recompute remains confined to collectReward and setDepletionDuration.

phUSD EMISSION: _updatePhUSDEmissionRate is called only from stake (:725), withdraw (:776), setDesiredAPY and setDepletionDuration — never from claim, never from _claimRewards, and never from claimUnclaimablePhUSD. Banking a payout cannot re-anchor the emission rate because it is not on any path that recomputes one.

BANK PULL: claimUnclaimablePhUSD (:644-651) calls neither _updatePool nor _updatePhUSDEmissionRate. It mints phUSD — the staking token — but minting does not change totalStaked, so the APY-driven rate (:985, a pure function of totalStaked and desiredAPYBps) is unaffected.

NO SCHEDULE COUPLING: unlike the stable stream (finite rewardBalance depleted over a window), phUSD emission is uncapped APY-driven minting with no distributable pool, so banking cannot return value to a pool and cannot re-anchor a window. Profile INV-05 confirmed.
refutations.pocEvidence: test_ECON003_valueConservation_noDoublePay — PASS. Tranche 2 accrues at the unchanged rate after tranche 1 was banked, and settles for exactly its own amount.

refutations.hypothesis: Task item 4 — a call path reaches _claimRewards WITHOUT the caller-side realignment at :715/:761/:808, or a banked amount is later paid a second time.
refutations.verdict: REFUTED — profile claim independently re-verified, and confirmed empirically. INV-02/INV-03 HOLD.
reasoning: CALLER COMPLETENESS: `grep -n _claimRewards src/PhlimboV3.sol` yields exactly three call sites — 708 (stake), 749 (withdraw), 806 (claim). All are internal-only (the function is `internal`), and each is followed by an UNCONDITIONAL realignment of all three debts to the full accumulator (715-717 / 761-763 / 808-810). There is no fourth path and no conditional skip of the realignment.

SUBTLETY CHECKED: at stake, _claimRewards is conditional (`if (userDetails.amount > 0)`, :707) but the realignment at :715-717 is NOT — it runs even when the claim was skipped, and it runs AFTER `userDetails.amount += amount` (:714), so the debt is set against the NEW balance. Pending settles to zero on both the paid and the banked path. Same shape at withdraw (realigned against `remaining`, including the dust-rule forced full exit).

NO DOUBLE-PAY: because the debt realigns identically whether the leg paid or banked, the same wei can never be both banked and later minted through a normal claim. The bank pull itself is CEI-correct (:647-648 zero the entry and decrement the aggregate BEFORE the mint at :649) and refuses a second pull with 'Nothing to claim'.

CROSS-CONTRACT LEG: MigratorV2V3's balance-delta accounting (:243/:260, `phUSDRewards = balanceOf(this) - phUSDBefore`) is CORRECT under banking — a banked mint produces no balance delta, so the migrator forwards nothing and cannot over-forward. Value conservation survives the migrator boundary (the migrator's failure mode is the STRAND of ECON-001, not a double-pay).
refutations.pocEvidence: test_ECON003_valueConservation_noDoublePay — PASS. Tranche 1 banked; a later successful claim pays EXACTLY tranche 2 and does not re-pay tranche 1; the bank pull then yields earned1+earned2 total, once each; a second pull reverts.

refutations.hypothesis: Task item 3 — a phUSD supply cap converts the fail-safe into an unbounded unpayable liability with a permanently-reverting pull path.
refutations.verdict: REFUTED — no cap exists. See headlineDeterminations.phUSDSupplyCap.
reasoning: FlaxToken.mint (lib/immutable/flax-token-v2/src/FlaxToken.sol:58-69) has exactly two requires (canMint, mintVersion match) and then OZ _mint. No cap, no ceiling.

The bank's ONLY trigger is de-authorization — setMinter(minter,false) or revokeAllMintPrivileges() (:88-91) bumping the global mintVersion and invalidating every minter at once. Both are owner-controlled and fully reversible via setMinter, which re-stamps the current mintVersion (:45-48).

Therefore the bank is always honourable once authority is restored, and the 'permanently-reverting pull' scenario cannot arise from a cap. The pull's revert-on-still-missing-authority is a recoverable state, not a terminal one (profile INV-06, their test_claimUnclaimablePhUSD_roundTrip).

protocolValueFlowSummary.storyO31NetAssessment: story-031 is economically NEUTRAL and correctly implemented. It closes the last propagating value-out leg in _claimRewards, defers rather than creates value, adds no wei to the phUSD mint surface, and preserves banked+paid==earned exactly. The three findings above are all consequences of WHERE the deferred obligation is recorded (an un-minted IOU keyed to `beneficiary`), not of how much it is worth.
protocolValueFlowSummary.deadCodeNote: At the shipped config the entire story-031 change is UNREACHABLE (desiredAPYBps == 0 => pendingPhUSDAmount == 0 => the :913 leg is never entered). This is correct, defensive future-proofing for a currently-dormant stream, and it is not itself a defect — but every finding in this scan inherits that dormancy, which is why all three are Low/QA rather than Medium.
assumptionGaps: SolvencyDetermination.md was read only via DEDUP-04's quoted §2 in the ledger; the full document was not re-read this run. The LEG-1 consistency argument rests on that quotation.

PhlimboV2's phUSD mint leg was NOT re-examined — story-031 touched only V3. A reverting mint inside phlimboV2.withdraw (MigratorV2V3.sol:250) still propagates and is absorbed by migrate's try/catch (skipping the user); that is pre-existing behaviour outside this diff.
The IPhlimboHook revert leg (profile deferredToInteractionAnalysis item 2) is a code-scanner/availability question, not an economic one, and was left to that agent.
